questions.prompt: Which function passes data from a parent down to a child component?
questions.explanation: input() declares a read-only property a parent binds data into; events flow back up via output().

options.text: An input and output pair bundled for two-way [(binding)]

questions.explanation: model() wires an input and matching output together so a value flows both directions via [(prop)].

questions.prompt: How should two completely unrelated sibling components share state?

options.text: By prop drilling through every ancestor
Through a shared injectable service, typically providedIn: 'root'

questions.explanation: Inputs/outputs only work parent-child; unrelated components inject the same singleton service and react to its signals.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid mutating an input() value directly inside a child?

options.text: input() is a read-only signal representing parent-owned data; mutating it breaks unidirectional data flow

questions.explanation: Use model() for shared two-way values or emit an output() and let the parent update its own state.

questions.prompt: When is viewChild() the appropriate tool?

options.text: For passing data down to a child
For imperative access to a child instance, like calling .focus() or .reset()

questions.explanation: viewChild() bypasses the input/output contract, so reserve it for genuinely imperative needs.

questions.prompt: Which variant of input() forces the parent to supply a value or fail at compile time (e.g. title = input.____<string>())?
questions.explanation: input.required<T>() fails fast at compile time instead of silently rendering with undefined.
